An action chunk contains several proposed commands, but a controller need not execute the entire chunk before obtaining a new prediction.
Prediction, execution, and feedback therefore have separate time scales.

## Horizon and feedback definitions {#horizons}

An observation horizon counts past observations provided to the policy.
A prediction horizon counts action positions in a predicted window; depending on its alignment, that window can include positions associated with observation history.
An execution horizon counts commands applied before switching to an updated plan.
In an asynchronous controller, the next result may be computed before the controller adopts it.
A training horizon is the segment length used in training, and an effective horizon concerns how far dependencies or rewards materially affect learning or behaviour.
These need not be the same number.

An open-loop segment executes a precomputed sequence without using new task observations to replan that segment.
A closed-loop policy updates decisions from feedback.
An action-chunk policy can be closed-loop across chunks while executing several commands open-loop within each chunk.
Its low-level motor controller may still use fast feedback throughout.
See [ACT](../../literature-review/action/act.qmd), [Diffusion Policy](../../literature-review/action/diffusion-policy.qmd), and [IRTC](../../literature-review/action/irtc.qmd#execution-timeline).

## From a valid chunk to continuous execution {#execution}

Generating a plausible chunk and switching safely between chunks are separate problems.
Two individually valid samples can choose incompatible strategies.
[ACT](../../literature-review/action/act.qmd) combines overlapping predictions through temporal ensembling.
[IRTC](../../literature-review/action/irtc.qmd) instead guides new generation using the previous chunk, with different weights for committed and overlapping future actions.

## Keep the clocks separate {#time}

Robot time orders the commands that affect the physical system.
Diffusion indices and flow time order internal computations that generate a predicted chunk.
An intermediate denoising state is not a command currently being executed.
[Generative sampling](generative-sampling.qmd#objects) defines those numerical objects.
For model-specific data flow, continue to [Diffusion Policy](../../literature-review/action/diffusion-policy.qmd), [π0](../../literature-review/action/pi0.qmd), or [π0.5](../../literature-review/action/pi05.qmd).
